problemTitle: Three jobs stand between you and your new life.
problemBody: A residence-and-work permit in Poland means a case that runs for more than a year, talks at the counter in Polish, and letters with deadlines counted from the day they arrive. Miss one and the application is left unexamined. Dossierly carries all three.

faq1a: A personal AI caseworker for life abroad. You get your own private agent that remembers your whole residence case: it prepares you for official appointments, interprets while you talk to the official, reads the letters that follow and counts the deadlines.
faq2a: No. Dossierly interprets and explains. It never gives legal or medical advice, and an interpret-only guard checks every turn.
faq3q: Which countries and offices are covered?
faq3a: Poland first: temporary residence and work at the Mazowiecki office in Warsaw. Germany and France are next. A country goes live only when its offices, letter types and deadline rules are covered from their sources.
faq4a: The official's side is Polish. You can speak English, Ukrainian, Hindi or Tamil, and the app itself can be shown in any of these four languages.
faq5a: No. Hindi and Tamil speech uses your browser's own recognition, and only the text is kept. Voice input in Polish, English and Ukrainian is switched off for now while we move it to a provider that keeps your audio private; you can type instead.
faq6q: What happens to my personal data?
faq6a: Your case lives in a private case file on Cloudflare, one per account, readable only when you are signed in. It is never sold, and you can have it deleted at any time. Identifiers are masked before any model call, and every model call is listed in your privacy ledger.
faq7a: Starting is free: your case path, the deadline calculator and 3 letters explained. One residence case is 199 zł once (18 months, nothing renews), or 399 zł a year for a household of up to four. An agency charges about 1,700 zł for the same case. See the pricing page.
